step_by_step_reasoning: We first identify the compute layer (OutSystems Platform) represented by the top box categorizing data. This is mapped to EC2. Next, we map the target storage and database services: S3 for binary data, Aurora Serverless for relational data, DynamoDB for key-value configuration, and Secrets Manager for sensitive credentials. Finally, we map the encryption layer, consisting of a central KMS node alongside two tenant keys (Tenant A, Tenant B) depicting Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) configurations that encrypt the target storage services.

graph.notes: OutSystems decomposes its data monolith by classifying data types (binary, relational, key-value, encrypted) and storing them in specialized AWS services (S3, Aurora Serverless, DynamoDB, Secrets Manager) secured via KMS tenant keys.
